newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbian police beat protesters, says opposition.
newsitem.headline: Serbian police beat protesters, says opposition.

text.p: Serbian police beat protesters on Tuesday in the provincial town of Smederevska Palanka where the opposition and ruling Socialists have formed rival municipal governments, an opposition official alleged.
Some 1,000 supporters of the opposition Zajedno (Together) coalition were attacked when their daily march encountered a police cordon, a Zajedno official told Reuters by telephone.
"The police attacked without provocation at all, beating everyone in sight, including women and children," he said.
The local head of Zajedno, Ljubisa Brkic, required medical treatment after he was hit on the chin and stomach, the official, who asked not to be named, said.
Several others suffered less serious injuries, he added.
The independent Beta news agency also reported the incident and said a Zajedno parliament member was beaten.
The report of police action followed the swearing in of rival municipal governments in Smederevska Palanka, located some 80 km (50 miles) south of the capital Belgrade.
Zajedno swore in a municipal council on Tuesday in Smederevska Palanka based on results of November local elections, which gave the opposition a narrow majority.
The Socialists inaugurated their own town council with a leftist majority based on a court annulment of the opposition victory.

Riot police refused to allow all the Zajedno council members and their supporters to enter the council building. Zajedno ended up holding its ceremony outside the building while the Socialists swore in their deputies.
There have been increasing reports of police violence against opposition protesters, who have held 10 straight weeks of demonstrations demanding the Socialists concede defeat in local elections.
The United States accused President Slobodan Milosevic's government on Monday of breaking a pledge not to use force against the peaceful demonstrations.
In Belgrade no violence was reported on Tuesday evening as thousands of protesters converged on the city centre for a daily opposition rally.
